cues.text: From the Sun, we begin our tour of the solar system.
cues.name: The Sun

cues.text: The Sun is our star: a glowing sphere of hot plasma whose gravity holds every planet in orbit.
cues.name: The Sun

cues.text: Closest to the Sun is Mercury, the smallest planet, moving quickly through intense heat and long cold nights.
cues.name: Mercury

cues.text: Next is Venus, bright in our sky, wrapped in thick clouds and a powerful greenhouse atmosphere.
cues.name: Venus

cues.text: Then comes Earth, our blue home, with liquid water, living systems, and one steady Moon.
cues.name: Earth

cues.text: Beyond Earth is Mars, the red planet, with dust storms, ancient river valleys, and the tallest volcano in the solar system.
cues.name: Mars

cues.text: Farther out is Jupiter, the largest planet, a giant world with storms, bands of clouds, and many moons.
cues.name: Jupiter

cues.text: Then Saturn appears, famous for its wide icy rings and soft golden color.
cues.name: Saturn

cues.text: Next is Uranus, a cold blue-green ice giant, tilted so far that it seems to roll around the Sun.
cues.name: Uranus

cues.text: At the edge of the major planets is Neptune, deep blue and windy, circling in the distant dark.
cues.name: Neptune

cues.text: Together they form our solar system: one star, eight planets, moons, rings, asteroids, comets, and the quiet rhythm of orbit.
cues.name: Solar System
